assessment.nobel_worthiness: The optical lattice clock combines Katori's magic-wavelength idea with Ye's demonstration of extreme coherence and systematic control. It is a clean case where a basic quantum effect, engineered in detail, redefined the limit of precision measurement. It is already used for tests of fundamental constants, relativistic geodesy and a candidate redefinition of the second. It is both original and lastingly important.
assessment.attribution: The two credited names are the natural pair. Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice in 2001-2003 and made the first demonstrations. Ye's group drove the record accuracy and stability and the many-body clock work. Credit is relatively uncontested, though a fair prize might also weigh the earlier optical-clock and frequency-comb groundwork, which the 2005 prize partly recognised.
assessment.maturity: Several independent laboratories (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE and others) have reproduced and surpassed each other at the 1e-18 level. Timing is good, and the discovery is robust and reproducible.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views the work as an incremental advance on optical frequency standards recognised in 2005 and on ion-clock work (2012 prize, Wineland).
Relative weighting of the Katori and Ye contributions versus other lattice-clock groups is my own judgement from memory and not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantum key distribution turned the foundations of quantum mechanics (entanglement, no-cloning, measurement disturbance) into a concrete information-theoretic protocol. BB84 and Ekert's entanglement-based E91 protocol opened a field with deployed systems and satellite links. The conceptual originality is high and the impact is lasting. It connects directly to the 2022 prize on entanglement and Bell tests.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard authored BB84 and Ekert independently proposed E91, linking security to Bell inequalities, so the three credited names form a coherent trio. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea is not on the list and is a historical complication, as is the contribution of device-independent security work. Within the supplied names, the trio is the fairest fit.
assessment.maturity: The protocol has been implemented widely (fibre, free space, satellite). Practical security against side-channel attacks is still being addressed, but the underlying idea has been confirmed for decades. Recognition is timely, although the 2022 prize may reduce the appetite for another quantum-information award.
uncertainties: Whether the committee considers this physics rather than computer science or cryptography.
Overlap with the 2022 prize may make a second award in the same area difficult.
Priority and credit for Wiesner's conjugate coding is outside the supplied credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with controlled parameters. They allowed the superfluid-Mott insulator transition and later single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy. The field gave a general quantum-simulation platform, a decisive extension of the 2001 and 1997 prize areas. Originality and impact are high, and these experiments show many-body physics that is hard to study elsewhere.
assessment.attribution: Zoller (with Jaksch and others) proposed the Hubbard-model realisation, and Greiner and Bloch performed the landmark Mott-insulator experiment and developed microscope techniques. Esslinger's work on fermionic Hubbard physics and Cirac's theory are also decisive, so five credited names compete for at most three slots. I pick the proposal and the first experiments, but the allocation is uncertain.
assessment.maturity: Results have been reproduced across many laboratories, and the interpretation is stable. Quantum-simulation advantage for open problems such as the doped Hubbard model is still developing, so some of the claimed promise remains ahead of us.
uncertainties: Five credited names compete for three places, and the omission of Esslinger or Cirac is a real attribution weakness.
The platform's uniqueness against analog quantum simulation in superconducting circuits and ion traps is still evolving.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The discovery of the Higgs boson at the LHC confirmed the mechanism of electroweak symmetry breaking and completed the Standard Model's particle content. It is an experimental achievement of the first rank, decisive and unambiguous. The prize for the theory was given in 2013, and the experimental half is a standing question for the committee.
assessment.attribution: A big-collaboration discovery with thousands of authors. The proposed trio reflects the founding leadership of ATLAS (Jenni, Della Negra) and CMS (Della Negra, Virdee). Gianotti was ATLAS spokesperson at the time of the announcement. Any selection is partly a judgement about leadership rather than a unique personal discovery, and the Nobel rule of three laureates makes this hard. I defer to colleagues on particle physics.
assessment.maturity: The discovery was announced in 2012, and the properties of the boson (couplings, spin-parity) have been steadily confirmed by both experiments. The result is mature and independently confirmed by two detectors.
uncertainties: Large-collaboration attribution under the three-person limit is unresolved and could be seen as arbitrary.
I am less well placed to judge particle-physics priorities than my colleagues, and I have not verified the leadership roles.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators, followed by experimental realisation in HgTe quantum wells and in Bi-Sb and Bi2Se3 surface states, created a new class of matter. It extended the 2016 topological-phase prize to time-reversal-symmetric systems. Originality, clarity and lasting impact are very strong.
assessment.attribution: Kane (with Mele) supplied the theory, Molenkamp (with Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, who are not credited here) the first experimental observation in HgTe, and Hasan the first 3D topological insulator in Bi-Sb. Mele is a co-author of the decisive theory and is left out, and the supplied list omits Zhang, so a fair configuration is hard. Condensed matter is outside my core area and I defer partly.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations and a large follow-up literature. The interpretation is well established, although practical applications are not yet realised.
uncertainties: Mele's coequal role in the Kane-Mele papers and the absence of the HgTe theory proposers from the credited list.
Overlap with B025, which would need to be resolved if both were considered.
Outside my specialisation.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at the magic angle and the 2018 observation of correlated insulators and superconductivity in twisted bilayer graphene opened moire quantum matter. It created a tunable platform with an immense follow-up literature. It is a clear case where a new regime of physics was opened, but it remains young.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald provided the theory (2011) and Jarillo-Herrero's group the experiments (with Cao and others, who are not on the list). The three credited names map onto theory and experiment in a natural way. Credit for the experiment may include Cao as lead author, which a three-person limit cannot represent.
assessment.maturity: Replicated by many groups, but the nature of the superconducting pairing and the correlated states is still debated. Prize timing may be premature relative to a stable understanding.
uncertainties: The pairing mechanism and phase diagram are unsettled.
Student and postdoc contributions to the key experiment fall outside the credited names.
Competing interest from related candidates B014 and B046 in 2D materials.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED turned superconducting circuits into controllable quantum systems that couple strongly to microwave photons, giving the dispersive readout and the architecture used in most superconducting quantum processors. It is a clean example of foundational quantum optics becoming an enabling platform. I know this area very closely, which is both a strength and a limitation.
assessment.attribution: Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf wrote the 2004 proposal, and Wallraff and Schoelkopf's groups did the strong-coupling experiment. The credited trio is a reasonable fit but omits Girvin and others, and the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling already honoured the superconducting-circuit field. I should note my own conflict of interest as a Chalmers/WACQT researcher and weigh my assessment with caution.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed by many laboratories and underpinning quantum processors. Timing is good scientifically, but the 2025 award makes an immediate second award in the same area a harder sell.
uncertainties: Close to my own research community, so my judgement may be biased and recusal could be needed.
Whether the committee wants to follow the 2025 prize with a related award so soon.
The fault-tolerant computing promise is still ahead of us.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Event Horizon Telescope's images of the M87* and Sgr A* shadows provide direct horizon-scale evidence for black holes and test general relativity in the strong-field regime. The result is striking and has big public impact. The scientific novelty is in the technique, VLBI at 1.3 mm, and the scale of the observation.
assessment.attribution: The project is a large collaboration of hundreds, with Doeleman as founding director, Falcke as the proposer of the shadow imaging concept and Narayan providing key accretion-flow modelling. Credit allocation is hard and arguably arbitrary among collaboration leaders. Outside my core expertise, so I defer to astrophysics colleagues.
assessment.maturity: Two sources imaged and later polarisation results, with consistent interpretations, but only one collaboration has produced the data. Independent confirmation is limited, so the work is somewhat early.
uncertainties: Single-collaboration data with limited independent replication.
The Nobel prize 2020 already recognised black-hole physics, which affects the balance across the field.
Allocation of credit among the leadership of a large collaboration is unresolved.
